title: Analytical Geometry: Equations of Lines and the Angle of Inclination
seo_title: Grade 11 Analytical Geometry Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Derive and apply the equation of a line through two given points, the equation of a line through one point and parallel or perpendicular to a given line, and the inclination (θ) of a line, where m = tan θ is the gradient of the line (0° ≤ θ ≤ 180°).
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 analytical geometry worksheets: equations of lines, parallel and perpendicular lines, and the angle of inclination. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Negative m: add 180° to the calculator angle.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) gives the line through (x₁; y₁) with gradient m.
  • Parallel lines: m₁ = m₂. Perpendicular lines: m₁ × m₂ = −1.
  • The angle of inclination θ is measured from the positive x-axis: tan θ = m.
  • If m is negative, θ = 180° + tan−1 m.

Examples

Example

m = −2

tan−1(−2) = −63,4°

Answer: θ = 116,6°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Negative mAdd 180° to the calculator answer.
The pointSubstitute x₁ for x and y₁ for y.
Perpendicularm₁ × m₂ = −1.

items.q: Find the equation of the line through (−3; 1) parallel to y = x − 4.
items.e: Parallel lines have equal gradients: m = 1. y − (1) = 1(x − (−3)), so y = x + 4.
